The find function can search recursively. But we want to list all files in /tmp. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will return all items. Or we can use ls with a=True but we need to specify path? There's no path param for ls. So we can't list /tmp directly. But we can use find. Let's call find with path="/tmp" and name="None"? Actually name defaults to "None" string. But we can pass name=None? The signature says name?: string, default: "None". So passing name=None might be okay. We'll do find({"path":"/tmp","name":"None"}). That should return all items. Then we can display them.
